newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Daschle sees budget amendment defeat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Daschle sees budget amendment defeat.

text.p: Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle said Monday he doubted Republicans would win the unanimous Senate support necessary to modify their proposed balanced budget constitutional amendment.
Daschle said he did not think the Senate would agree to give Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott permission to change the amendment as he suggested on CBS television's Face the Nation.

"The whole process would have to start over again," Daschle, a South Dakota Democrat, said at his regular press briefing. The Senate is to vote on the amendment Tuesday, and barring a last minute change of mind by Democrats, it is expected to fail.

"It is going to take more than just fringe cosmetics to deal with the balanced budget differently than we have," Daschle said. Lott said he might offer changes to permit the government to run a deficit during economic downturns.

Democratic opponents of the amendment are thought to have the 34 votes necessary to block its passage with the decisions last week of two freshmen Democrats, Robert Torricelli of New Jersey and Tim Johnson of South Dakota, to oppose it.

The amendment requires the government to balance its budget each year during peacetime starting in 2002 or two years after it becomes law. It needs a two-thirds vote in the House and Senate to pass and then must be ratified by 38 of 50 states.
